question.text: In a trust-structured AIF, the person who settles the initial trust property and triggers formation of the trust by executing the trust deed is called the:

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that a trust AIF requires a settlor to settle the trust, and that the settlor is the author of the trust who conveys the initial sum to the trustee. The trust deed is then used to appoint the Trustee. The Trap: Option A (custodian) safekeeps securities. Option B (Investment Manager) manages investments under the IMA, not the formation of the trust. Option C (fund administrator) keeps books and records. None of these settles the trust. Note: Source pages 138 and 343 support the settlor's role as the author of the trust who settles the initial sum.
